# ThemeScript

Sets `data-theme` on `<html>` before the first paint, so a stored dark preference never flashes light. Render it once, in the server-rendered root `<head>`.

```tsx
import { ThemeScript } from "@ouro.bot/ui/theme";
```

## Example

```tsx
<html suppressHydrationWarning>
  <head>
    <ThemeScript />
  </head>
  <body>…</body>
</html>
```

## Usage

`suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>` is required: the script adds `data-theme` before React hydrates, and React would otherwise report the extra attribute as a mismatch. Do not render it in client-only trees, where React warns about client-rendered scripts.

`"system"` removes the attribute, which lets `color-scheme: light dark` follow the OS. A stored value other than `light`, `dark` or `system` is ignored in favor of `defaultTheme`.

Set the scheme on the root, as this script does: `data-theme` on `<html>` (or the OS setting) always works, even when your CSS pipeline lowers `light-dark()` for older browsers. A dark scheme set on a wrapper (`style={{ colorScheme: "dark" }}`) needs native `light-dark()` support, because lowered tokens resolve once at the root.

## Props

Type: `ThemeScriptProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultTheme` | `"light" \| "dark" \| "system"` |  | Used when nothing valid is stored. `"system"` follows the operating system. |
| `nonce` | `string` |  | CSP nonce for the inline script, for apps with a strict Content-Security-Policy. |
| `storageKey` | `string` |  | The localStorage key that holds `"light"`, `"dark"` or `"system"`. |
